model.line: On the block drawn on the Qing plan S01: position and frontage from the plan, heights and roof from the typology of its hall class, its form drawn by the hall kit. It will be updated as the research goes on.
rows: platform 0.7 m, eave 4.4 m, ridge 6.46 m above the ground
hip-and-gable 歇山, rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile

by the hall kit: 5 bays, the middle widest, a porch front, steps on the front, left, 歇山 hip-and-gable with a rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile, a painted beam under the eave. Drawn from the typology of its hall class, not from a picture of this hall (assumed, C).

evidence.title: 敷春堂: centre of the palace block
evidence.summary: Centre of the block inside the gate, the dowager's residence in Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, rear part garden. In 1860 only 18 bays of duty rooms, tea and meal kitchens and a pharmacy survived. That supports reading 药房 for the third label of QC71.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.
